google2025.name: Google 2025 Environmental Report (66% hourly carbon-free energy in 2024)

guardianDrought.name: The Guardian (Milman & Witherspoon), analysis of 809 planned US data centers using Cleanview and NIDIS drought data; republished by Mother Jones

utilization.unit: average IT draw as a fraction of IT capacity
utilization.locator: p. 49, Server Electricity Use: AI servers average 60-80% of rated power, operating 75-85% of the year
utilization.derivation: low = 0.60 x 0.75, high = 0.80 x 0.85. Ignores idle draw during non-operating hours, so the low end is conservative.

evaporative.label: Cooling towers, all year
evaporative.description: Water-cooled chillers with cooling towers running year-round. Heat leaves by evaporating water.
evaporative.locator: Figure 4.4 (p. 46), large-scale rows 'Waterside economizer (water-cooled chiller)' and 'IT Liquid cooling: waterside economizer (water-cooled chiller)'; range spans both rows' whiskers
evaporative.derivation: Values read off a box-plot figure by eye (about +/-0.02 PUE, +/-0.05 WUE). The low end is a best-practice facility in a favorable climate; the high end is poor efficiency in a hot, humid climate.

hybrid_air.label: Outside air + water on hot days
hybrid_air.description: Outside air does most of the cooling; water is evaporated (adiabatic assist or cooling towers) only when it's hot.
hybrid_air.locator: Figure 4.4 (p. 46), large-scale rows 'Airside economizer & adiabatic cooling (air-cooled chiller)' and '(water-cooled chiller)'; range spans both rows' whiskers
hybrid_air.derivation: Values read off a box-plot figure by eye. LBNL notes (p. 47) its simulation probably understates this design's water use: some hyperscale operators report 0.1-0.3 L/kWh for similar systems, versus near 0 simulated for the air-cooled-chiller variant.

closed_loop.label: Closed-loop (liquid to dry coolers)
closed_loop.description: Liquid-cooled IT rejecting heat through dry coolers, with an air-cooled chiller as backup. No evaporative water in normal operation.
closed_loop.locator: Figure 4.4 (p. 46), large-scale row 'IT Liquid cooling: dry cooler (air-cooled chiller)'
closed_loop.derivation: Values read off a box-plot figure by eye. NOTE FOR REVIEW: in LBNL's simulation this configuration's PUE is NOT higher than evaporative. The energy penalty the brief describes shows up mainly for air-cooled IT on mechanical chillers (see 'air').

air.label: Air-cooled (no evaporative water)
air.description: Air-cooled IT with outside-air economizer and air-cooled chillers. No cooling tower and no adiabatic assist.
air.locator: Figure 4.4 (p. 46), MIDSIZE row 'Airside economizer (air-cooled chiller)' -- LBNL does not simulate a purely waterless air-cooled configuration for large-scale facilities
air.derivation: Values read off a box-plot figure by eye. Midsize facilities have lower UPS/airflow efficiency (Table 4.3), so a large facility likely sits toward the low end.

immersion.label: Immersion
immersion.description: Servers submerged in dielectric fluid, rejecting heat through dry coolers. Higher up-front cost.
immersion.locator: Table 4.2 (p. 42) groups immersion with direct-to-chip under 'IT liquid cooling'; values reuse Figure 4.4's 'IT Liquid cooling: dry cooler (air-cooled chiller)' row
immersion.derivation: LBNL does not model immersion separately, and no peer-reviewed measured annual PUE for immersion was found while drafting. Same numbers as closed-loop until a better source is added. The up-front cost difference is not modeled.

coolingShares.locator: Figure 4.2 (p. 39), 'Data center cooling systems distribution by space category in 2023', Hyperscale and AI Specialized bars
coolingShares.derivation: LBNL estimated these splits from Dell'Oro Group equipment-sales data plus industry expert input (p. 38). Read off a stacked bar chart by eye (about +/-3 points), then grouped: towers all year = waterside economizer + water-cooled chiller + IT liquid waterside economizer; outside air + water on hot days = airside economizer & adiabatic (both chiller types) + airside economizer (water-cooled chiller) + dry cooler with adiabatic assist; fans/AC = airside economizer (air-cooled chiller) + air-cooled chiller + direct expansion + dry cooler; closed loop = IT liquid dry cooler with and without adiabatic assist. LBNL doesn't track immersion separately.

plannedInDrought.note: Planned facilities in areas that were in drought at some point in the past year.

topStates.locator: p. 37: Virginia hosts the highest data center electricity demand, followed by California and Texas

averageNewMW.note: Average size of data centers coming online; 2025 value reported as 'nearly 80 MW'. FERC's MW may measure whole-facility capacity rather than the computers' capacity the simulator's size slider uses, so the comparison is approximate.

operatingGW.note: 'More than 50 GW' operating at end of 2025.

ownPlants.note: Behind-the-meter (own power plant) projects, all fuels; Cleanview gives no fuel split. 'More than 25%' of all planned U.S. data center capacity.

contracts.note: Annual matching claims from the arXiv paper's table; Google's hourly carbon-free share counts all carbon-free sources (including nuclear and hydro), not only wind and solar.

futureBuildUncertainty.locator: p. 44: 'For future years, 2024-2028, the PUE and WUE values for the data center space types were varied by a range of +/- 10%'
futureBuildUncertainty.derivation: For build years from 2024 on, the low end shrinks by 10% and the high end grows by 10%. LBNL's projected fall in fleet-average PUE comes from fleet mix shifting to hyperscale, not from per-facility improvement, so no per-facility efficiency trend is applied.

gridCarbonTrajectory.locator: Table 18 'Total Electric Power' CO2 (million metric tons) / Table 8 'Total Net Electric Power Sector Generation' (billion kWh)
gridCarbonTrajectory.derivation: Low end = eGRID2023 subregion rate x (AEO intensity in build year / AEO intensity in 2025). High end = no decline (U.S. power-sector CO2 rose about 4% in 2025, and the AEO baseline excludes policy not yet in force). Applied to CO2e only; generation water is held at the 2023 mix.

generationWaterGalPerMWh.locator: Table 2 (non-renewable) and Table 1 (renewable), operational CONSUMPTION medians
generationWaterGalPerMWh.derivation: eGRID's resource mix doesn't say which cooling technology each fuel's plants use, so low = once-through-cooled median and high = cooling-tower median for that fuel's dominant technology. Hydropower reservoir evaporation is EXCLUDED: Macknick reports 1,425-18,000 gal/MWh depending on how a reservoir's evaporation is allocated, and they leave it out of their own figures for that reason.

oil.basis: no oil factor in Macknick; uses natural gas steam (once-through 240, tower 826) as the closest steam-cycle analog

gas.basis: natural gas combined cycle: once-through 100, tower 205

geothermal.basis: lowest/highest median across flash and binary configurations (EGS excluded)

otherFossil.basis: treated as natural gas combined cycle

unknown.basis: treated as natural gas combined cycle

grid.label: Regional grid
grid.description: Draws from the local eGRID subregion's actual 2023 generation mix.

onsite_gas.label: On-site gas plant
onsite_gas.description: A dedicated natural gas combined-cycle plant beside the facility.
onsite_gas.co2Derivation: heat rate 7,146-7,549 Btu/kWh (EIA: 2020 average operating heat rate; 2023 tested heat rate) x 116.65 lb CO2/MMBtu. Combustion CO2 only -- excludes upstream methane leakage, so this undercounts relative to eGRID's CO2e.
onsite_gas.waterDerivation: Macknick Table 2 NGCC: dry-cooled median 2, cooling-tower median 205.

dedicated_renewables.label: Wind/solar contract
dedicated_renewables.description: A power purchase agreement for wind and solar that matches the facility's annual consumption.
dedicated_renewables.derivation: Low end = the contracted wind/solar itself (about 0 CO2, 0-5 gal/MWh). High end = the local grid: annual matching doesn't cover the hours the wind and sun aren't there, and in those hours the facility physically runs on the grid mix. Where a given contract falls depends on hourly matching and additionality, which the operator rarely discloses.

capacityPriceUsdPerMWDay.note: PJM capacity prices, used as an illustrative benchmark for the yearly cost of one megawatt of generating capacity. Other regions price capacity differently or not at all. Transmission upgrades are not included and are often larger.

residentialShareOfSales.note: Stands in for the residential class's share of socialized costs. Real allocators use peak-demand-based factors set in rate cases.

defaultResidentialCustomers.note: Illustrative default for a mid-sized utility. The user can change it.

householdWater.note: Used only to translate onsite water into a familiar scale.

householdElectricity.note: Used only to translate electricity into homes' worth. Counts utility purchases, so it slightly understates use in homes with rooftop solar.

passengerVehicle.note: Used only to translate emissions into cars' worth. Tailpipe CO2 only.

contestedEvidence.finding: Looking back at 2015–2024, places that added data centers saw average home electricity rates fall slightly, not rise. Virginia, where data centers use over 20% of the power, tracked the national average.
contestedEvidence.limits: Only looks backward, mostly at the years before the 2025–26 AI building boom.

contestedEvidence.finding: Projected that wholesale electricity prices (what utilities pay power plants) could rise 6–29% nationally by 2030, and up to 57% in the hardest-hit regions.
contestedEvidence.limits: Wholesale prices aren't your bill. They make up only 30–50% of a typical home's bill.

contestedEvidence.finding: A viral '267% increase' figure was about wholesale prices, not what households pay each month.
contestedEvidence.limits: It corrects one claim. It doesn't show the impact is zero.

contestedEvidence.finding: Data centers are one cause among several, alongside equipment costs, aging power lines, and clean energy requirements.
contestedEvidence.limits: It's hard to pin rising bills on any one cause, and single-cause stories are wrong in both directions.
